missionPremise: Two live defects share one cause: the account has no readable entitlement without a parcel, and the billing interval is stored nowhere. Settings passes a null parcelNodeId on purpose because it is account-scoped, and GET /entitlement returned early without one, so Settings read Access as "Not read" for every account including paying ones. functions: configuredPeTierPriceIds(interval) — private; builds the configured set for one interval by calling stripePriceIdForPeTier for all three tiers, so exactly ONE place in the file knows which env name carries which (tier, interval) pair. Unset and blank env values are dropped by that accessor and never enter the set.
peBillingIntervalForPriceId(priceId) — the inverse of stripePriceIdForPeTier. Returns 'month' | 'year' | null.

peBillingIntervalFromPriceItems(items) — resolves a subscription's billed line items. Skips items matching nothing configured (the $25 extra-seat line is a real price but not a tier BASE price), refuses on two items that disagree, returns null when nothing matches.
failClosedCases: price id matching no configured id -> null, never 'month'
nothing configured at all (missing env group) -> null for every id, never 'month'
price id configured under BOTH a monthly and an annual env name -> null; we cannot tell which the customer was billed under and a guess is a fabricated billing fact
null / undefined / empty / whitespace price id -> null
two billed items resolving to different intervals -> null, not the first one
inverseMapping.whyNotAStripeApiField: Deliberately avoids current_period_end, price.recurring.interval and plan.interval. Their shapes track the Stripe API version and this repo pins no version anywhere — a separate unresolved problem the dispatch names. A price id is an opaque identifier we chose and put in env ourselves, so inverting it reads a source we control.
inverseMapping.whyNotOurOwnMetadata: pePaywallStripe.ts already writes metadata[billing_interval] at checkout and it is always present, which makes it tempting. Rejected: metadata is what we ASKED Stripe for, the price id is what Stripe BILLED. Persisting the request as though it were the billed fact is the fabrication this column exists to prevent. Pinned by the test 'P-98 VIOLATION: metadata[billing_interval] alone does NOT set the column'.

webhookWrite.mechanism: No new write path. The interval rides on the EXISTING setPeAccessTierFromStripe call that already writes the tier, via a new optional `billingInterval` parameter on that function (artifacts/api-server/src/lib/peIdentity.ts).
webhookWrite.oneReadOfTheItems: `peBilledPriceItems` reads the billed items once; `peGrantBillingFacts` derives BOTH the seat count and the interval from that one reading, so the two facts can never disagree about what was on the subscription.
webhookWrite.deliberateBehaviourChange: The conditional subscription fetch that already existed here for Team seats had its condition widened from 'team only' to 'any PE subscription grant whose payload carries no items'. REASON: Stripe never expands line_items on a checkout.session.completed webhook, so without the widening every new Solo and Studio subscriber would store a null interval — starving the exact rung the column was added to feed. It CANNOT change the seat count (resolveTeamSeatsPurchased returns null on its first line for any non-team grant) and costs at most one extra Stripe call per new subscription, inside the existing try/catch. Verified it adds no network calls to the existing suite: no current webhook test payload sets `subscription` on the session object.
webhookWrite.churnClears: tier 'free' writes billingInterval null, never omitting the column. A leftover 'month' after churn or a plan change is a silent false claim about the customer's billing — the same rule the seat count already follows.
webhookWrite.reDerivedOnEveryUpdate: customer.subscription.updated re-derives rather than carrying a value forward. A monthly-to-annual switch IS this event; a stale 'month' surviving it is the single worst output this column can produce, because it makes the rail upsell annual billing to somebody who just bought it.

deliverable2_entitlementWithoutAParcel.changedPaths: EXACTLY ONE: authenticated caller, no parcelNodeId.
deliverable2_entitlementWithoutAParcel.howTheGuardWasSplit: origin/main had one compound condition `(!authenticated || !userId || !parcel)`. It is now two: the anonymous check first and alone, then the parcel-absent check. Splitting it this way is what keeps anonymous callers byte-identical AND preserves guard precedence — on main an anonymous caller never reached the validity check, so an anonymous request with a malformed parcel returned 200 with today's body, not 400. That is pinned by a test rather than left to the reader.

shapeWithAParcel.howGuaranteed: The base literal was extracted verbatim into peEntitlementBaseBody and the route still spreads it followed by `property`, so insertion order — and therefore JSON.stringify output — is unchanged. Pinned by a full-string comparison against a literal transcribed from origin/main, not from the code under test.

shapeWithoutAParcel.why: An omitted block and a block full of falsy values are different facts. `"property" in body` is asserted false, not `toBeUndefined()`, because res.json drops an explicit undefined and a body carrying `property: undefined` would pass the weaker check while being the wrong construction.

deliverable2_entitlementWithoutAParcel.anonymousCallers: Unchanged in every case, with or without a parcel: they get today's base body. They have no account, so seatsPurchased and billingInterval would be meaningless. This is narrower than a literal reading of the dispatch's 'without one, return the account block' and is called out here rather than buried — it keeps a second response shape from moving.
deliverable2_entitlementWithoutAParcel.howTheFieldsAreRead: getPeEntitlementRow's SELECT and PeEntitlementSnapshot were widened, so the account answer costs no second query. Safe because the snapshot's consumers were ENUMERATED, not assumed: resolvePeEntitlement has exactly two (this route and brokerageNodeFacets.callerGrantsOwnerFact, which reads only snap.subscriptionTier) and neither spreads it into a response body. artifacts/smartsite-mcp keeps a private copy of the row reader and was not touched.
deliverable2_entitlementWithoutAParcel.devRole: resolvePeEntitlement already elevates tier and subscriptionTier for dev role. seatsPurchased and billingInterval are passed through UNELEVATED — an operator account bought nothing, and inventing billing facts for it is precisely what this column exists to prevent. Pinned by a test.

A test labelled 'VIOLATION: a blank env var cannot be matched by a blank price id' was VACUOUS: two independent guards produce that outcome and the input-side empty-string check satisfies it alone, so the assertion never exercised the config-side filter it appeared to be about. LESSON: A 'VIOLATION:' label on a test is a claim, not a property. Two independent guards can produce one outcome, and the cheaper guard satisfies the assertion alone — so the test never exercises the mechanism it appears to be about. Injecting the defect PER GUARD rather than per file is what distinguishes them. Instance: 'a blank env var cannot be matched by a blank price id' stayed green against a defect that admitted unset env vars into the configured set, because the empty-input check short-circuits first. Caught only because the falsifier was pre-registered per-defect.

In this repo, a DB-free unit test seam exists and is already established: `vi.mock("@workspace/db", () => ({...}))` with a FACTORY and no importActual, in a colocated src/lib/*.unit.test.ts. The precedent is peTeamSeatsFromStripe.unit.test.ts. The 165 api-server test files that fail without DATABASE_URL almost all use `vi.importActual` inside the mock factory, which re-enters the real module and constructs the Pool — that is the discriminator, not the presence of vi.mock. This is the difference between writing a violation test and OBSERVING one.

Reading a command's exit code through a pipe reports the LAST stage's status. `npx tsc -b lib/db 2>&1 | grep -v 'npm warn'; echo $?` printed 1 because grep matched nothing, and tsc had exited 0. Redirect to a file and read $? directly. Same family as the positional-formatter trap already in ENFORCEMENT.md.

Stripe does NOT expand line_items on a checkout.session.completed webhook payload. Anything derived from billed price items at checkout time needs the subscription fetched, or it is null for every new subscriber — a starved column that reports as a shipped feature.

lib/db/drizzle/README.md requires claiming a migration number free across main AND unmerged branches, not the next after your own base. `gh pr diff <n> --name-only` per open PR plus a `git ls-tree` sweep over unmerged remote branches is the check.

pg_dump renders a table CHECK constraint inside the CREATE TABLE body, alphabetically by constraint name, as `CONSTRAINT name CHECK (((col IS NULL) OR (col = ANY (ARRAY['a'::text, 'b'::text]))))`. A hand-patch of the LDT schema fixture must match byte-for-byte; nine existing constraints of that shape are in the file to copy from.

Rejected deliberately, with a test pinning that metadata alone does not set the column, so nobody re-derives it as an easy win.
